title: Ecclesiastes Bible Quiz - Chapter 10
description: Ten questions on Ecclesiastes 10: dead flies in the perfumer's oil, the blunt ax, wise and foolish words, and a bird that may carry your voice.

questions.text: What do dead flies cause the oil of the perfumer to produce?
questions.explanation: Dead flies cause the oil of the perfumer to produce an evil odor; so does a little folly outweigh wisdom and honor.

questions.text: Where is a fool's heart, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: A wise man's heart is at his right hand, but a fool's heart at his left.

questions.text: What should you do if the spirit of the ruler rises up against you?
questions.explanation: If the spirit of the ruler rises up against you, don't leave your place, for gentleness lays great offenses to rest.

questions.text: What has the speaker seen concerning servants and princes?
questions.explanation: The speaker has seen servants on horses, and princes walking like servants on the earth.

answers.text: Servants ruling cities and princes in prison
Servants on horses and princes walking like servants
Servants sleeping and princes keeping watch

questions.text: What may happen to him who digs a pit?
questions.explanation: He who digs a pit may fall into it, and whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.

answers.text: He may find a treasure in it
He may be injured by stones
He may grow weary and stop

questions.text: If the ax is blunt and one doesn't sharpen the edge, what must he do?
questions.explanation: If the ax is blunt and one doesn't sharpen the edge, then he must use more strength; but skill brings success.

answers.text: He must buy a new ax

questions.text: What are the words of a wise man's mouth like, in contrast to a fool?
questions.explanation: The words of a wise man's mouth are gracious, but a fool is swallowed by his own lips.

questions.text: When is a land called happy, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: Happy are you, land, when your king is the son of nobles, and your princes eat in due season, for strength and not for drunkenness.

answers.text: When its king is a child
When its princes eat in the morning
When its king is the son of nobles
When its people feast every day

questions.text: What happens to the roof through slothfulness?
questions.explanation: By slothfulness the roof sinks in, and through idleness of the hands the house leaks.

answers.text: The roof is carried off by the wind
The roof is covered with grass

questions.text: Why should you not curse the king, even in your thoughts?
questions.explanation: Don't curse the king in your thoughts, nor the rich in your bedroom, for a bird of the sky may carry your voice, and that which has wings may tell the matter.

answers.text: Because the king's servants stand at every door
Because the king knows the hearts of all men
Because a bird of the sky may carry your voice
